author: Akien
prose:
AKIEN, 2026-08-11, verbatim, across four turns of one design conversation.

--- (1) what the harbor master is, correcting CC's read ---

"almost. fleet register yes. owns the space the gates live in and the trickets ride thru. reports on the status of the items just mentioned. but it's not the authority. it's not the rules. the rules are on the ticket. truth comes from certifications that an item has passed a gate. Harbor Master was a week of you and I arguing about the details I just spelled out. you can read the chat logs if you're not sure. grep for the beginning of 'harbor master'. and you tried then to imbue it with rules and authority then too. the rules are in the inspectors. the tickets are owned by the intentions. the harbor is the pipeline workspace. and right now there's one worker, you. so of course very little works. but this is the foundation the rest of it needs. and it's all a peer system with no managers. well, except me."

--- (2) no controller for mail; and WHAT IS A GATE ---

"have a little more first: i didn't ship postmaster you did. for me i don't see a reason for a controller there. if i push mail into the system (create a record in the db) the next time the reciever's shim looks for messages it finds it. all done? now what i am confused by is this: what is a gate? it should be a class, and we should instantiate a gate and an inspector for each gate. the harbor master will need to have probes on the gates. so the gate instance hands messages to the harbor master at each transition. that allows the harbor master to recieve that information. the probes are on the gates. now how does that work? that should be wherever the gates are represented in our trees yes? i expect it's something like .cairn/devices/device/0/tools/gate/2/probes <- and that is probably in the runtime trees added when the gate instance is constructed. what do you think?"

--- (3) killing CC's claim that a probe must be code in git ---

CC had written: "the probe's definition is code and stays in class-space beside the gate - otherwise it's not in git". Akien:

"why? because the only other option is the database? said while standing in the middle of scads of json files that address keeping information in git all around you? it just becomes runtime config :)"

--- (4) ratifying one CC suggestion ---

"gates with names instead of numbers: perfect"

--- CC's contributions inside this conversation, marked so a later reader can tell spec from translation ---

RATIFIED by (4): name the gate instance rather than number it - tools/gate/buildme_entry/probes, not tools/gate/2/probes - because a number makes a reader memorise a mapping and the probe's whole question is about THAT gate.

NOT YET RULED, CC's reading, offered in the same conversation and not responded to: (a) an INSTRUMENT (the ~30 lines that read a trace and count door_pass vs send_back) is genuinely code and belongs beside what it measures, while the probe proper (trigger threshold, enough, to, nexus, why, carried text) is declaration - so the split is instrument-vs-declaration, not probe-vs-config; (b) git holds the seed dial and the runtime tree holds the current one, so the delta between them IS what the gate learned, and today that delta cannot exist because there is only one copy and it is a Python literal; (c) when the gate hands the harbor master a message at each transition, that message is a NOTIFICATION and not the record - the crossing stays in the boat's own history, or the register stops being an index and becomes a rival record.
